title: Permitting Coordinator
description:
Remote Raven is recruiting a full-time, fully remote Permitting Coordinator on behalf of our client, a fast-growing US roofing and exteriors group that runs a family of regional brands across the Eastern and Central United States. The group operates a portfolio of regional roofing brands and completes a high volume of residential and commercial roofing work every year, all of which is regulated at city, county and state level.
The Permitting Coordinator owns the full lifecycle of permit acquisition and compliance across every one of the group's branded entities. You are the central liaison between municipalities, internal teams, homeowners and contractors, and you are responsible for making sure every project meets local, county and state regulatory requirements. You maintain the records, you make the inspections happen on time, and you provide the administrative and operational backbone of permitting across new installations, repairs and warranty work.
This is a role of consequence rather than volume alone. A permit that lapses before its final inspection creates a compliance problem for the brand and a property-record problem for the homeowner, and it does so silently. The person who succeeds here is the one who treats an open permit as unfinished business until the day it is closed.
Key Responsibilities
Permit Application & Expediting

• Prepare, apply for, and expedite permit applications for roofing projects across all of the group's branded entities.

• Identify the correct permitting authority for each project address, including the distinction between an incorporated city and the unincorporated county surrounding it.

• Assemble complete application packets: scope of work, project documentation, contractor license and registration details, certificates of insurance, and bonds where the jurisdiction requires them.

• Submit applications through each jurisdiction's channel, whether that is an online portal, an email intake address, or a phone-and-fax counter.

• Push stalled applications forward: follow up on review times, answer plan-reviewer questions, and resolve corrections and resubmittals.

Tracking, Renewals & Inspections

• Maintain a comprehensive tracking system covering every open permit across every brand and jurisdiction, with status, dates, fees, and next action visible at a glance.

• Ensure timely renewals so that no permit lapses while a job is still open.

• Schedule and confirm final inspections, and confirm every inspection requirement is completed before the permit expires.

• Track failed inspections through to a passed re-inspection, including routing correction notices to the right project manager and rescheduling.

Municipal & Internal Liaison

• Act as the primary point of contact between local authorities and project managers on all permit matters.

• Call, email, and follow up with city, county, and state building departments during their business hours.

• Coordinate with project managers, field crews, the licensing team, and subcontractors to gather the documentation each application requires.

• Communicate professionally with homeowners and public officials, representing the brand on every contact.

Compliance Review

• Review project plans, scopes, and supporting documentation to confirm they meet local permitting and zoning requirements before submission.

• Compile and maintain current knowledge of municipal code years, permit requirements, fee schedules, and inspection protocols for every jurisdiction the group works in.

• Flag scopes that will not pass review as written, before they become a rejected application and a delayed crew.

Close-Out & Problem Resolution

• Own each permit through to close-out, so that jobs finish with a passed final inspection and a closed permit on record.

• Address expired permits by reapplying, resolving outstanding fees, and scheduling follow-up inspections.

• Escalate blockers early and in writing, with the specific action needed and from whom.

The role

Job Description
A bit about this role:
The analysis behind Devoted's Medicare Advantage portfolio - which markets to grow in, which products to invest in, which benefit designs and cost structures actually work, creating those benefits - is driven today by a very small number of people. This team sits between claims analytics, product strategy, engineering, and actuarial, and is rebuilding how the portfolio and bid cycle work using agentic workflows and AI-assisted pipelines.
This is not a reporting role. You'll own the strategic thinking and the pipework underneath it, often on the same day - there's no analyst between you and the data - and you'll see the whole picture - we'll expect you to have an opinion about it.
Your Responsibilities and Impact will include:

• The analysis behind portfolio decisions . Product and service area mix - where we push growth and where we protect margin. You won't always be handed a question list; you'll help decide which questions matter.

• Cost and utilization work that answers the actual question . Decompose PMPM trend into utilization versus unit cost, build comparison groups you can defend when someone attacks them, and honestly size what a benefit change or network change will really do to claims.

• Independent financial judgment on benefit designs . Our own estimate of what a design does to revenue and cost, plus a clear sense of how much weight that estimate can bear. You'd own that work and be direct about its limits.

• Recommendations leadership can act on . Present data-backed recommendations to senior leaders regularly, including the CEO, and defend them live.

• Building the infrastructure, not just using it . We're rebuilding how the portfolio and bid cycle work with agentic workflows, AI-assisted code generation, and automated pipelines that turn what used to be weeks of manual work into something that runs overnight. This team is at the center of that build, and you'll push these tools into territory nobody here has tried yet.

• Go-to-market support . Once plans are filed, build the analyses go-to-market runs on, supporting marketing, sales, and brokers with a clear read on where our plans compete well and who they're built for.

• AEP monitoring . Track enrollment as it comes in against what the bid assumed: volume by plan and county, product mix, and the profile of who's choosing us. When something is moving the wrong way, you're the one who catches it early enough for us to do something about it.

• Being the person people come to . When someone needs to know whether a metric is built the right way or whether the data is being read correctly, you're the answer, not a ticket to another department.

Required skills and experience:

• Six or more years in Medicare Advantage with your hands in the data . You know how claims are structured, what place-of-service and revenue codes tell you, the difference between allowed and paid, how completion factors work, and how risk adjustment feeds into all of it. You've been burned by a bad pull before, and you know what you check now because of it.

• Cost and utilization analytics . PMPM trend broken into utilization versus unit cost, clean comparison groups, sizing the impact of a benefit or network change. You know the difference between a number that moved and a number that means something.

• Strong SQL and real comfort in a large claims warehouse (Snowflake, Databricks, or similar).

Brief info about Vinted 

Our mission is to make second-hand the first choice, and we're looking for people who want to help us get there. Every day, we work together to help our members buy and sell pre-loved clothing and lifestyle items, giving each piece a second life - or even a third.
The Vinted Group is made up of three business units that support this mission:

Vinted Marketplace is Europe’s leading platform for second-hand fashion and a go-to destination for all kinds of pre-loved items, with a growing range of categories. Our platform connects millions of members across 20+ markets, helping great items find a new life.

Vinted Go enhances the shipping experience with a vast network of over 500,000 pick-up and drop-off points, partnering with more than 60 carriers across Europe, with added services like item verification for peace of mind on high-value pieces.

Vinted Pay is the newest part of the Vinted Group, dedicated to bringing secure, reliable payments to buyers and sellers across Europe. Seamlessly integrated into the Vinted app, it helps keep every transaction safe, efficient, and easy for our members.

Founded in 2008 in Lithuania, Vinted began as a way for friends to find new homes for clothes they no longer needed. In 2019, we became Lithuania's first unicorn! Today, our headquarters remain in Vilnius, and we've grown with offices across Europe, supported by a team of over 2,000 people. 

Information about the position 

We are looking for an Engineering Manager to lead GRC and Assurance in Group Security: a team of seven today, growing even more in 2027. The team owns risk management, compliance and audit liaison, second-line security assurance, AI governance, third-party risk, business continuity and security culture.

Vinted spans three distinct entities: Marketplace, Vinted Go, and Vinted Payments, our regulated payments institution. That means handling a fast-moving regulatory landscape covering core privacy (GDPR, CCPA), payment licenses, incoming mandates like DORA, NIS2, and the EU AI Act, alongside driving our 2027 ISO 27001 certification. In most companies, governance runs quietly in the background. At Vinted, it’s core architecture.

We are looking for a practitioner rather than a documenter: someone who leads from the front, turns requirements into controls that work, and grows the people around them through hands-on work.

In this position, you’ll 

• Deliver ISO 27001 by 2027: Own the scope, audits, and a single control set covering NIS2 and DORA (with PCI DSS managed separately).

• Map our compliance stack: Build the master map across all three businesses (what applies, when, and liability) to unblock key decisions.

• Run governance like engineering: Turn controls into code, automate evidence, and serve as the first user for Group Security’s new posture platform.

• Lead and grow the team: Manage seven functions, develop specialists on Lead Implementer/Auditor tracks, and add three new hires through early 2027.

About you 

• You have run a security governance or compliance function through a certification or a regulator's examination, ISO 27001 or something comparable.

• You think like an engineer about governance: you can say how a control can be automated and how evidence gets collected without a spreadsheet.

• You can hold several regimes in your head at once and tell a real obligation from an assumed one.

• You develop specialists rather than delivering around them, and you will say something is not compliant when nobody wants to hear it.
